summary.en-US: See who follows you back on X (Twitter): Mutual, Follows you or Doesn't follow you, next to every name. Private, no tracking.
summary.it: Scopri chi ti ricambia su X (Twitter): Vi seguite, Ti segue o Non ti segue, accanto a ogni nome. Privato, nessun tracciamento.

description.en-US: X shows "Follows you" on profiles, but not where you actually read: the timeline. Nod fixes that. Next to the name of every author, Nod adds a small label: • Mutual: you follow each other • Follows you: they follow you, you don't follow them • Doesn't follow you: they don't follow you, whether or not you follow them It works in your Home timeline, in replies, in search and on profiles, in light, dim and dark mode. The labels follow your X language (English and Italian today). Private by design Nod only reads the information X already sends to your browser. It makes no requests of its own, stores nothing, has no account, no analytics and no tracking. Everything happens in the tab you are looking at. Nod is an independent project and is not affiliated with X Corp.
description.it: X mostra "Ti segue" sui profili, ma non dove leggi davvero: nel timeline. Nod risolve questo. Accanto al nome di ogni autore, Nod aggiunge una piccola etichetta: • Vi seguite: vi seguite a vicenda • Ti segue: ti segue, ma tu non lo segui • Non ti segue: non ti segue, che tu lo segua o no Funziona nel timeline Home, nelle risposte, nella ricerca e sui profili, nei temi chiaro, dim e scuro. Le etichette seguono la lingua di X (per ora inglese e italiano). Privacy prima di tutto Nod legge solo le informazioni che X invia già al tuo browser. Non fa richieste proprie, non salva niente, non ha account, analytics né tracciamento. Tutto avviene nella scheda che stai guardando. Nod è un progetto indipendente e non è affiliato a X Corp.

release_notes.en-US:
The grey “Doesn't follow you” pill now appears for everyone X identifies as a non-follower. Hover over it to see whether you follow them: “You follow them, but they don't follow you” or “Doesn't follow you, and you don't follow them”.

Your own posts stay unlabeled. Nod recognizes your signed-in account from X's page data at any window width, without reading cookies.

version.approval_notes:
content.js is bundled (not minified) with Vite from the TypeScript sources in the attached source archive. To rebuild: Node.js 24+, then `npm ci && npm run build`; the add-on is output to dist/firefox. Full instructions are in README.md, section "Build for AMO reviewers".

How it works: the content script runs in the MAIN world on x.com only. It passively reads the JSON responses that X's own web client already downloads (XMLHttpRequest/fetch to /i/api/), extracts the per-user `followed_by` / `following` flags, and inserts a small label next to the author's name. To leave the user's own posts unlabeled, it reads the signed-in account's id (`session.user_id`) from X's inline `window.__INITIAL_STATE__` script, or the handle from X's profile link in the side navigation. It makes no network requests of its own, uses no storage and declares no permissions.
